Component contract

Purpose: · semantic HTML · attributes · variants/sizes · states ·

Every Squircle component obeys this contract. Read it before adding or changing a component. Stages 3+ implement against it; tests enforce the mechanical parts (naming, token references, documented-class coverage).

1. Naming

  • sq-<component> for the block (.sq-button, .sq-panel, .sq-card).
  • sq-<component>--<variant> for variants and sizes, double hyphen

(.sq-button--primary, .sq-button--large).

  • sq-<component>__<element> for internal parts, double underscore

(.sq-button__icon, .sq-panel__header). Parts are never used alone; they inherit the block's context.

  • Utilities (sq-p-md, sq-hidden) compose with components but never

replace them: state, semantics, and accessibility live in the component.

2. Semantics first

  • The HTML element carries the meaning; classes carry the appearance.

Actions are <button>, navigation is <a href>, headings are h1–h6.

  • Never use an anchor as a button or a button as a link. Never add ARIA

that duplicates native semantics (role="button" on a <button> is a defect, not diligence).

  • Icon-only controls MUST have an accessible name (aria-label);

decorative icons MUST be hidden (aria-hidden="true", focusable="false").

  • Disabled is disabled (form controls) or aria-disabled="true" plus

non-activation (links — see LINKS.md). Never communicate state by color alone: pair every color cue with text, shape, or position.

3. States

Every interactive component specifies, implements, and tests: default, hover, :focus-visible, active, disabled, and loading/busy where it can occur. :focus-visible is always the 3px azure ring (or the theme's focus token) — components never remove or restyle it into invisibility. All motion honors prefers-reduced-motion.

4. Tokens and theme behavior

  • Components reference semantic or component-tier tokens — never brand

hex, never another component's tokens.

  • No Luca-specific values in generic rules. A component must render

correctly under any theme that passes checkThemeContrast; Luca and Ocean are both tested.

  • Customization precedence (verified by cascade test in components.spec.ts):
  1. Framework defaults (this layer).
  2. Active theme tokens (:root / [data-sq-theme]).
  3. Component variant defaults (.sq-button--primary, …).
  4. Consumer overrides (later stylesheets, higher-or-equal specificity).

Qualifications: variant defaults (3) beat theme tokens (2) where the variant's appearance is its own defaults (shape, spacing, ring) — text, radius, and spacing still follow the theme. Fills that DERIVE from a semantic token follow the theme's retune of that token: Ocean retunes --sq-color-accent, so accent-derived fills (primary button, switch track, tab indicator) ride along; tokens Ocean does not retune (danger red, success green) keep their values. Consumers (4) win by source order at equal specificity; Squircle never uses !important, so one consumer rule always suffices.

5. Spacing and density

  • Internal padding, gaps, and section rhythm come from --sq-space-*.

Comfortable defaults are the DEFAULT — there is no compact density.

  • Related elements group tightly (2xs–sm); content groups separate

(md–lg); sections separate generously (section token).

  • Long labels wrap; controls never clip text. Minimum target height for

interactive controls is 44px (Squircle default: 48px/3rem, 40px/2.5rem for sm size only where justified).

  • Every component passes the §8.6 density gate at 360/768/1024/1440 in

both Luca and Ocean before it is marked complete.

6. Responsive behavior

  • Components reflow or stack; they never squeeze. Breakpoint-specific

changes use the documented responsive utilities or component rules — never duplicated ad-hoc media queries per instance.

  • Touch targets stay ≥44px on coarse pointers; hover-only affordances

always have a touch/keyboard path.

6b. Motion

  • Durations and easings come from the motion tier (five durations,

instant→slower; four easings) or an established component-duration token (--sq-spinner-speed, --sq-skeleton-shimmer-duration). No literal ms/s timing outside the base gate (enforced by packages/css/test/motion.test.ts).

  • Reduced motion is gated exactly once, at the base layer: all

animation-* and transition-* collapse to a 0.01ms no-op and scroll-behavior becomes instant. Components never re-gate globally; per-component PRM blocks only harden layer specifics (carousel instant scroll, shimmer/spinner rest states, switch thumb) or are unnecessary because motion survives as state feedback (instant-duration transitions).

  • Keyframes live in the sq- namespace; author-facing entries

(.sq-fade-in, .sq-rise-in, .sq-hover-lift, .sq-active-press, .sq-motion-none) ride the same tokens.

  • New components land motion-silent by default: toggles/openers flip

via hidden, animations must state a reason. If a transition is justified, it starts at --sq-motion-duration-quick with --sq-motion-easing-out and gets no special PRM treatment — the base gate already covers it.

7. Documentation requirements (per component)

Purpose · semantic HTML · attributes · variants/sizes · states · accessibility guidance · theme behavior · customization · responsive notes · common mistakes · tested limitations. Examples in docs MUST be copy-pasteable and MUST match the implementation (the coverage test fails otherwise).
